title: IMPROVE Bleeding Risk Score
sources: Decousus H et al. Chest 2011 (IMPROVE); ASH 2018 VTE prophylaxis guideline
purpose: Estimates in-hospital major and clinically relevant bleeding risk in acutely ill MEDICAL inpatients. Pair with a VTE risk score (Padua / IMPROVE VTE): a score ≥ 7 (or key single risk factors) marks the patient in whom pharmacologic prophylaxis may do more harm than good — use mechanical prophylaxis instead.

items.label: Bleeding in the 3 months before admission

interpretation.label: Not increased bleeding risk (< 7) — major bleeding risk ~ 0.4%, any clinically relevant bleeding ~ 1%. Pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis is appropriate if VTE risk warrants it
Increased bleeding risk (≥ 7) — major bleeding ~ 4%+, clinically relevant bleeding ~ 8%+. Prefer MECHANICAL prophylaxis (IPC); reassess for pharmacologic prophylaxis once the bleeding risk resolves

notes: Points include half-values (e.g. active GD ulcer 4.5) — do not round the inputs. Any of active GD ulcer, recent bleeding, or platelets < 50 alone is a strong contraindication to pharmacologic prophylaxis regardless of total. The IMPROVE VTE companion score (different weights) sits on the other side of this decision.
